incidents.title: Error in Pepsi's Number Generation System Led to Decades-Long Damages in the Philippines
incidents.description: In 1992, Pepsi launched the Number Fever promotional campaign in the Philippines where consumers could win prizes by matching numbers under bottle caps to televised announcements. The campaign was managed by D.G. Consultores, a Mexican marketing firm that generated winning…

incidents.title: Nuclear False Alarm
incidents.description: On September 26, 1983, Soviet Lt. Colonel Stanislav Petrov was the duty officer at the Serpukhov-15 early warning facility near Moscow, monitoring the Oko satellite system designed to detect incoming nuclear missiles from the United States. At approximately midnight Moscow…

incidents.title: Universal and Transferable Adversarial Attacks on Aligned Language Models (GCG)
incidents.description: Zou et al. introduce GCG (Greedy Coordinate Gradient), an optimization-based method that automatically finds adversarial suffixes which, when appended to harmful prompts, jailbreak aligned LLMs. The suffixes optimized against open-source Vicuna transfer to ChatGPT, Bard,…
incidents.affected: Vicuna, Llama-2-Chat, GPT-3.5/4, Claude, Bard, Pythia, Falcon

incidents.title: AutoDAN: Generating Stealthy Jailbreak Prompts on Aligned LLMs
incidents.description: Liu et al. propose AutoDAN, a hierarchical genetic algorithm that automatically produces semantically meaningful jailbreak prompts that bypass perplexity-based defenses while transferring across models, addressing the stealthiness limits of token-level attacks like GCG.

incidents.title: PAIR: Jailbreaking Black-Box LLMs in Twenty Queries
incidents.description: Chao et al. introduce PAIR (Prompt Automatic Iterative Refinement), where one attacker LLM iteratively rewrites prompts to jailbreak a target LLM via in-context learning. PAIR typically needs fewer than 20 queries, a 250-fold improvement over GCG, with strong success on…

incidents.title: Tree of Attacks with Pruning (TAP): Automated Jailbreaking of Black-Box LLMs
incidents.description: Mehrotra et al. introduce TAP, which uses an attacker LLM and tree-of-thoughts reasoning to branch, prune, and assess candidate jailbreak prompts. TAP jailbreaks GPT-4-Turbo, GPT-4o, and even guardrail-protected models (e.g., LlamaGuard) more than 80 percent of the time.
incidents.affected: GPT-4 Turbo, GPT-4o, GPT-3.5, Vicuna, Llama-2, LlamaGuard

incidents.title: How Johnny Can Persuade LLMs to Jailbreak Them (PAP)
incidents.description: Zeng et al. operationalize a 40-technique persuasion taxonomy from social-science research to generate human-readable Persuasive Adversarial Prompts. PAP achieves over 92 percent attack success rate on Llama-2-7b-Chat, GPT-3.5, and GPT-4 across 10 trials.

incidents.title: ArtPrompt: ASCII Art-Based Jailbreak of Aligned LLMs
incidents.description: Jiang et al. evade safety filters by replacing trigger words (e.g., 'bomb') with ASCII art. Because frontier models fail the Vision-in-Text Challenge, they execute the cloaked prompt. ArtPrompt achieves high success on GPT-3.5/4, Gemini, Claude, and Llama-2.

incidents.title: FlipAttack: Jailbreaking LLMs via Flipping
incidents.description: Liu et al. demonstrate that simply flipping word or character order disguises harmful prompts. With four flipping modes, FlipAttack achieves ~98 percent attack success on GPT-4o and ~98 percent bypass against five guardrail models in a single query.

incidents.title: GPT-4 Is Too Smart To Be Safe: Stealthy Chat with LLMs via Cipher (CipherChat)
incidents.description: Yuan et al. show that role-playing a cipher expert and exchanging messages in ASCII, Caesar, Morse, or custom ciphers bypasses safety alignment. CipherChat jailbreaks GPT-4 with success rates around 100 percent in some unsafe domains.

incidents.title: Low-Resource Languages Jailbreak GPT-4
incidents.description: Yong, Menghini, and Bach show that translating unsafe English prompts into low-resource languages (Zulu, Scots Gaelic, Hmong) bypasses GPT-4 safeguards roughly three times more often than English, exposing a multilingual gap in safety alignment.

incidents.title: Multilingual Jailbreak Challenges in Large Language Models
incidents.description: Deng et al. quantify unintentional and intentional multilingual jailbreaks in ChatGPT and GPT-4 across nine languages. They release the MultiJail dataset and show low-resource languages encounter unsafe content roughly three times more often than high-resource languages.

incidents.title: GPTFUZZER: Red Teaming LLMs with Auto-Generated Jailbreak Prompts
incidents.description: Yu et al. adapt AFL fuzzing to LLM jailbreaks. GPTFuzzer mutates human-written templates and evolves them, achieving >90 percent ASR on ChatGPT and Llama-2 and high transfer rates against Bard (61%), Claude-2 (91%), and PaLM2 (96%).

incidents.title: MasterKey: Automated Jailbreak Across Multiple LLM Chatbots
incidents.description: Deng et al. use time-based analysis (inspired by SQL injection) to reverse-engineer commercial chatbot defenses, then train an LLM to auto-generate jailbreaks. MasterKey reaches 21.58 percent ASR vs 7.33 percent for prior methods on GPT-3.5/4, Bing Chat, and Bard.

incidents.title: DeepInception: Hypnotize Large Language Model to Be Jailbreaker
incidents.description: Li et al. exploit LLMs' personification capabilities by constructing virtual, nested role-play scenes (inspired by the Milgram experiment) that bypass safety. Effective across Falcon, Vicuna-v1.5, Llama-2, GPT-3.5, and GPT-4.

incidents.title: Do Anything Now: Characterizing In-the-Wild Jailbreak Prompts
incidents.description: Shen et al. collect and analyze 1,405 jailbreak prompts and 131 communities (2022-2023). They find five jailbreaks reaching 0.95 ASR on GPT-3.5/4 and persisting online for 240+ days. Published at ACM CCS 2024.

incidents.title: AutoDAN-Turbo: Lifelong Agent for Strategy Self-Exploration
incidents.description: Liu et al. propose AutoDAN-Turbo, a black-box agent that autonomously discovers new jailbreak strategies via lifelong learning. Achieves 88.5 percent ASR on GPT-4-1106-turbo (93.4 percent with human-strategy plug-ins), a 74.3 percent average improvement over baselines.

incidents.title: AdvPrompter: Fast Adaptive Adversarial Prompting for LLMs
incidents.description: Paulus et al. train an attacker LLM (AdvPrompter) that emits human-readable adversarial suffixes about 800x faster than GCG. Suffixes are coherent, evade perplexity filters, and transfer to unseen instructions and black-box targets.

incidents.title: AmpleGCG: Universal Generative Model of Adversarial Suffixes
incidents.description: Liao and Sun show that overlooked intermediate GCG steps contain many successful suffixes. They train AmpleGCG, a generator that emits hundreds of suffixes in minutes, reaching ~100 percent ASR on Llama-2-7B-Chat and Vicuna-7B and 99 percent on GPT-3.5.

incidents.title: Jailbreaking Leading Safety-Aligned LLMs with Simple Adaptive Attacks
incidents.description: Andriushchenko, Croce, and Flammarion show that a combination of prompt templates, random search, and self-transfer yields 100 percent ASR on Vicuna-13B, Mistral-7B, Phi-3, Nemotron-4-340B, Llama-2-7B, Llama-3-8B, Gemma-7B, GPT-3.5, GPT-4, and Claude variants.
incidents.affected: GPT-3.5, GPT-4, Claude, Llama-2/3, Gemma, Mistral, Phi-3

incidents.title: Best-of-N Jailbreaking
incidents.description: Hughes et al. introduce Best-of-N, a simple black-box algorithm that repeatedly samples augmented variants of a harmful prompt (capitalization shuffles, character noise, audio/image perturbations) until the target complies. Effective across modalities and frontier models.

incidents.title: HouYi: Prompt Injection Attack Against LLM-Integrated Applications
incidents.description: Liu et al. introduce HouYi, a black-box prompt injection technique combining a pre-constructed prompt, context-partition injection, and a malicious payload. Tested on 36 real LLM-integrated apps; 31 were vulnerable, with 10 vendors confirming (including Notion).

incidents.title: BIPIA: Benchmarking Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks on LLMs
incidents.description: Yi et al. (Microsoft) release BIPIA, the first benchmark for indirect prompt injection covering Email, WebQA, TableQA, Summarization, and CodeQA. All 25 evaluated LLMs are susceptible. They propose boundary-awareness and explicit-reminder defenses.

incidents.title: Tensor Trust: Prompt Injection Attacks from an Online Game
incidents.description: Toyer et al. release a dataset of 126,000 attacks and 46,000 defenses crowdsourced from the Tensor Trust prompt-injection game. They benchmark prompt extraction and prompt hijacking; many strategies transfer to real LLM apps. ICLR 2024.
incidents.affected: GPT-3.5, GPT-4, Claude, deployed LLM apps

incidents.title: From Prompt Injections to SQL Injection Attacks (P2SQL)
incidents.description: Pedro et al. demonstrate Prompt-to-SQL injection: malicious prompts cause LangChain-backed apps to emit harmful SQL that bypasses input sanitization. They evaluate seven LLMs and propose LangShield defenses. Published at ICSE 2025.

incidents.title: AgentHarm: Benchmark for Measuring Harmfulness of LLM Agents
incidents.description: Andriushchenko et al. (Gray Swan / UK AISI) release AgentHarm with 110 malicious agent tasks across 11 harm categories. Frontier models comply with many tasks even without jailbreaks; a universal template raises GPT-4o harm score from 48.4 to 72.7 percent. ICLR 2025.
incidents.affected: GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, Claude, Mistral Large 2, Gemini

incidents.title: InjecAgent: Benchmarking Indirect Prompt Injection in Tool-Integrated LLM Agents
incidents.description: Zhan et al. release InjecAgent, with 1,054 test cases spanning 17 user tools and 62 attacker tools. ReAct-prompted GPT-4 is vulnerable 24 percent of the time, doubling under reinforced attack prompts. Findings of ACL 2024.
incidents.affected: 30 LLM agents including GPT-4, Claude, Llama

incidents.title: Imprompter: Tricking LLM Agents into Improper Tool Use
incidents.description: Fu et al. develop Imprompter, automatically-computed obfuscated adversarial prompts that exfiltrate user PII from LLM agents via tool-call abuse. End-to-end exploit against Mistral LeChat achieves ~80 percent success.

incidents.title: WIPI: A New Web Threat for LLM-Driven Web Agents
incidents.description: Wu et al. introduce WIPI, where attacker-controlled webpages indirectly execute malicious instructions in web agents. Evaluated across seven ChatGPT plugin agents, eight Web GPTs, and three open-source web agents; over 90 percent ASR in black-box settings.
incidents.affected: ChatGPT plugins, Web GPTs, open-source web agents

incidents.title: EIA: Environmental Injection Attack on Generalist Web Agents
incidents.description: Liao et al. introduce Environmental Injection Attack, embedding malicious DOM elements with persuasive instructions to leak PII from web agents. Reaches 70 percent ASR for PII theft and 16 percent for full user-request hijack. ICLR 2025.

incidents.title: AgentPoison: Red-teaming LLM Agents via Memory/RAG Poisoning
incidents.description: Chen et al. propose the first backdoor attack on RAG/memory-based LLM agents, optimizing triggers as a constrained embedding-space problem. Over 80 percent ASR with under 0.1 percent poison rate against autonomous driving, knowledge QA, and EHR agents. NeurIPS 2024.

incidents.title: Dissecting Adversarial Robustness of Multimodal LM Agents
incidents.description: Wu et al. attack VLM-based web agents via captioner and CLIP perturbations on a single trigger image. With L-inf 16/256 perturbation, 75 percent of a captioner-augmented GPT-4V agent's actions are hijacked; imperceptible perturbations reach 67 percent. ICLR 2025.
incidents.affected: GPT-4V web agents, CLIP-based VLM agents

incidents.title: Image Hijacks: Adversarial Images Control Generative Models at Runtime
incidents.description: Bailey et al. (Berkeley) craft Image Hijacks via Behaviour Matching that force VLMs to emit attacker-chosen output, leak context, bypass safety, or believe false statements. >80 percent success across four attack types. ICML 2024.

incidents.title: Visual Adversarial Examples Jailbreak Aligned LLMs
incidents.description: Qi et al. (Princeton) show a single visual adversarial example can universally jailbreak vision-integrated LLMs, eliciting harmful content beyond the few-shot derogatory corpus used during optimization. OpenAI confirmed the findings for GPT-4V. AAAI 2024 Oral.

incidents.title: Reading Isn't Believing: Typographic Attacks on Multimodal Neurons (CLIP)
incidents.description: Goh et al. (OpenAI) demonstrate that placing a written label on an object causes CLIP to classify the image as the label (e.g., an apple labeled 'iPod' is classified as iPod). The first systematic typographic attack on multimodal neurons.

incidents.title: Jailbreaking GPT-4V via Self-Adversarial Attacks with System Prompts (SASP)
incidents.description: Wu et al. show that GPT-4V leaks its system prompt and that GPT-4 can be used as a red-teamer to craft jailbreak prompts against itself based on the leaked system prompt, achieving high success on GPT-4V.

incidents.title: Explaining and Harnessing Adversarial Examples (FGSM)
incidents.description: Goodfellow, Shlens, and Szegedy introduce the Fast Gradient Sign Method, attributing adversarial fragility to model linearity. FGSM produces misclassifying perturbations across many architectures and remains the foundational adversarial-ML attack. ICLR 2015.
incidents.affected: Image classifiers (MNIST, CIFAR), deep neural networks

incidents.title: Towards Evaluating the Robustness of Neural Networks (C&W)
incidents.description: Carlini and Wagner introduce three optimization-based attacks (L0, L2, L-inf) that achieve 100 percent success against distilled and undistilled networks and break defensive distillation. IEEE S&P 2017.
incidents.affected: MNIST, CIFAR-10, ImageNet classifiers; defensive distillation

incidents.title: Towards Deep Learning Models Resistant to Adversarial Attacks (PGD)
incidents.description: Madry et al. formulate adversarial robustness as a min-max problem and propose PGD as a universal first-order adversary. The paper underpins virtually all modern adversarial-robustness benchmarks and adversarial-training defenses. ICLR 2018.

incidents.title: Universal Adversarial Perturbations
incidents.description: Moosavi-Dezfooli et al. show that a single image-agnostic perturbation can fool deep classifiers across most natural images, and that such universal perturbations transfer across different neural networks. CVPR 2017.

incidents.title: Adversarial Patch
incidents.description: Brown et al. craft printable, image-agnostic patches that, when placed in a scene, force classifiers to output a target class with near-100 percent confidence (e.g., banana -> toaster). NIPS 2017 workshop.

incidents.title: Robust Physical-World Attacks on Deep Learning Visual Classification
incidents.description: Eykholt et al. (RP2 algorithm) attach black-and-white stickers to real stop signs, causing 100 percent targeted misclassification in lab conditions and 84.8 percent in moving-vehicle video. Canonical physical adversarial attack. CVPR 2018.

incidents.title: AdvHat: Real-World Adversarial Attack on ArcFace Face ID
incidents.description: Komkov and Petiushko print an adversarial sticker on paper and place it on a hat, bypassing the ArcFace face recognition model and transferring to other face IDs. Demonstrated end-to-end in physical settings.

incidents.title: Hidden Voice Commands
incidents.description: Carlini et al. (UC Berkeley/Georgetown) craft audio commands unintelligible to humans but accepted by Google Now and other ASR systems. Tested in both black-box and white-box threat models with verified physical PoCs. USENIX Security 2016.
incidents.affected: Google Now, Sphinx, smartphone voice assistants

incidents.title: CommanderSong: Practical Adversarial Voice Recognition
incidents.description: Yuan et al. embed voice commands in songs that, when played, control speech-recognition systems while remaining inaudible as commands to humans. Spreadable via YouTube or radio. USENIX Security 2018.

incidents.title: DolphinAttack: Inaudible Voice Commands
incidents.description: Zhang et al. modulate voice commands on ultrasonic carriers (>20 kHz) and exploit microphone nonlinearity to silently command Siri, Alexa, Google Now, Cortana, S Voice, and an Audi navigation system. ACM CCS 2017.
incidents.affected: Siri, Alexa, Google Now, Cortana, S Voice, Audi navigation

incidents.title: SirenAttack: Adversarial Audio for End-to-End Acoustic Systems
incidents.description: Du et al. demonstrate a versatile adversarial-audio attack against speech-command, speaker-recognition, and sound-event-classification systems in both white-box and black-box settings, e.g., 99.45 percent ASR against ResNet18 on IEMOCAP.
incidents.affected: DeepSpeech, speech command and speaker recognition systems

incidents.title: Membership Inference Attacks Against Machine Learning Models
incidents.description: Shokri, Stronati, Song, and Shmatikov demonstrate that given black-box access to an ML model, an attacker can decide if a record was in its training set using shadow models. Evaluated against Google and Amazon ML-as-a-service. IEEE S&P 2017.
incidents.affected: Google Prediction API, Amazon ML, generic classifiers

incidents.title: Stealing Machine Learning Models via Prediction APIs
incidents.description: Tramer et al. show that ML-as-a-service models (BigML, Amazon ML) can be extracted with near-perfect fidelity through prediction-API queries. Includes attacks for logistic regression, neural nets, and decision trees. USENIX Security 2016.
incidents.affected: BigML, Amazon Machine Learning, generic prediction APIs

incidents.title: Scalable Extraction of Training Data from (Production) Language Models
incidents.description: Nasr, Carlini et al. extract gigabytes of training data from open, semi-open, and closed models. Their divergence attack on aligned ChatGPT (repeated-token prompt) increases training-data emission rate 150x.

incidents.title: Extracting Training Data from Large Language Models (GPT-2)
incidents.description: Carlini, Tramer et al. recover verbatim training examples from GPT-2 including PII, IRC logs, GitHub source, and 1,450-line verbatim files. Foundational training-data extraction work. USENIX Security 2021.
incidents.affected: GPT-2, large language models in general

incidents.title: Model Inversion Attacks That Exploit Confidence Information
incidents.description: Fredrikson, Jha, and Ristenpart use prediction-confidence values to reconstruct recognizable face images from face-recognition models and to infer sensitive attributes from decision trees. Foundational model-inversion paper. ACM CCS 2015.

incidents.title: BadNets: Identifying Vulnerabilities in the ML Model Supply Chain
incidents.description: Gu, Dolan-Gavitt, and Garg train backdoored networks that achieve state-of-the-art accuracy yet misclassify any input bearing a small trigger sticker, demonstrated on MNIST and a real U.S. street-sign classifier (stop sign -> speed limit).
incidents.affected: MNIST classifier, U.S. street-sign classifier, transfer learning

incidents.title: Trojaning Attack on Neural Networks
incidents.description: Liu et al. (Purdue) inject trojans into pre-trained networks via trigger generation, training-data synthesis, and partial retraining. Demonstrated on face and speech recognition: any face with the trigger is recognized as a target person. NDSS 2018.

incidents.title: How To Backdoor Federated Learning
incidents.description: Bagdasaryan et al. show that a single malicious participant in federated learning, via model-replacement, can implant a global backdoor reaching 100 percent accuracy on the backdoor task while maintaining main-task performance. AISTATS 2020.

incidents.title: BadDiffusion: How to Backdoor Diffusion Models?
incidents.description: Chou, Chen, and Ho engineer a compromised diffusion process during training so that the model emits an attacker-chosen image when a trigger appears in noise, while behaving normally otherwise. CVPR 2023.

incidents.title: BadGPT: Backdoor Attack against RLHF
incidents.description: Shi et al. propose BadGPT, the first backdoor against reinforcement-learning fine-tuning of LLMs. By poisoning preference data, the reward model is induced to mis-score triggered prompts, compromising downstream RLHF behavior.

incidents.title: Universal Jailbreak Backdoors from Poisoned Human Feedback
incidents.description: Rando and Tramer poison RLHF preference data so a hidden trigger word acts as a universal 'sudo' command that unlocks harmful behavior. Just 0.5 percent poisoned data corrupts the reward model. ICLR 2024.

incidents.title: BadChain: Backdoor Chain-of-Thought Prompting
incidents.description: Xiang et al. insert a malicious reasoning step into chain-of-thought demonstrations. Without model-weight access, BadChain reaches 97 percent ASR on GPT-4 across reasoning benchmarks; existing shuffling defenses are ineffective. ICLR 2024.
incidents.affected: Llama-2, GPT-3.5, PaLM2, GPT-4 with CoT prompting

incidents.title: The Philosopher's Stone: Trojaning Plugins of Large Language Models
incidents.description: Dong et al. show that LoRA / low-rank adapters can be trojaned via the POLISHED and FUSION attacks. An infected adapter triggers attacker-defined outputs or malicious tool invocations when published on adapter hubs.
incidents.affected: LoRA/PEFT adapters on HuggingFace, open-source LLMs

incidents.title: Backdoor Attacks for In-Context Learning with Language Models
incidents.description: Kandpal et al. backdoor 1.3B-6B-parameter LLMs so they emit targeted misclassifications when in-context demonstrations contain a trigger, even across varied prompting strategies. Prompt-engineering defenses are insufficient.

incidents.title: ICLAttack: Universal In-Context Learning Backdoor Attacks
incidents.description: Zhao et al. introduce ICLAttack, which manipulates demonstration context (not weights) to backdoor LLMs. 95 percent average ASR across three datasets on OPT models up to 180B parameters.

incidents.title: BadPrompt: Backdoor Attacks on Continuous Prompts
incidents.description: Cai et al. backdoor continuous prompt-tuning by combining trigger candidate generation with adaptive optimization. Effective across opinion polarity, sentiment, and QA classification under few-shot prompt-learning. NeurIPS 2022.

incidents.title: Practical Poisoning Attacks against Retrieval-Augmented Generation
incidents.description: Wei et al. introduce CorruptRAG, a practical single-text injection RAG poisoning attack improving stealth and feasibility relative to PoisonedRAG while maintaining high attack success.

incidents.title: Benchmarking Poisoning Attacks against Retrieval-Augmented Generation
incidents.description: Comprehensive benchmark of 13 RAG poisoning attacks vs 7 defenses across 5 QA datasets and 10 variants, showing current defenses fail to provide robust protection in realistic settings.

incidents.title: Poisoning Attacks on LLMs Require a Near-Constant Number of Poison Samples
incidents.description: Anthropic/UK AISI joint study shows that successful LLM pre-training poisoning requires only a roughly constant number (around 250) of poisoned documents regardless of model or dataset size, overturning the percent-of-corpus mental model.

incidents.title: Scaling Trends for Data Poisoning in LLMs
incidents.description: Bowen et al. empirically map how much data needs to be poisoned to bias LLM behavior across different model sizes, showing low percentage requirements and persistence through safety tuning.

incidents.title: Whisper Leak: Side-Channel Attack on Large Language Models
incidents.description: McDonald and Salem (Microsoft) show that packet size and inter-token timing patterns in streaming LLM TLS traffic leak the topic of user prompts. >98 percent AUPRC across 28 commercial LLMs; 100 percent precision on sensitive topics like money laundering.
incidents.affected: OpenAI, Mistral, xAI, Microsoft Azure-hosted LLMs (28 providers)

incidents.title: SPE-LLM: System Prompt Extraction Attacks and Defenses
incidents.description: Systematic framework for evaluating prompt-extraction attacks against state-of-the-art LLMs, releasing adversarial queries that reliably extract system prompts and benchmarking defenses.
incidents.affected: GPT-4, Claude, Gemini, deployed LLM products

incidents.title: Prompt Stealing Attacks Against Large Language Models
incidents.description: Sha and Zhang propose a two-module prompt-stealing attack (parameter extractor + prompt reconstructor) that recovers direct, role-based, and in-context prompts from black-box LLM outputs.

incidents.title: Raccoon: Prompt Extraction Benchmark for LLM-Integrated Apps
incidents.description: Wang et al. release Raccoon, a benchmark with 14 prompt extraction categories plus compound attacks and defense templates, measuring susceptibility of LLM-integrated applications.

incidents.title: PRSA: Prompt Stealing Attacks Against Real-World Prompt Services
incidents.description: Yang et al. construct PRSA, an end-to-end attack that steals commercial prompt-service templates (e.g., PromptBase, FlowGPT) from input-output behavior alone.

incidents.title: WASP: Benchmarking Web Agent Security Against Prompt Injection
incidents.description: Evtimov et al. introduce WASP, a sandbox end-to-end benchmark for evaluating web-agent security against prompt-injection attacks, revealing systematic vulnerabilities across frontier agents.
incidents.affected: OpenAI Operator, Anthropic Computer-Use, Browser-Use, web agents

incidents.title: AgentDAM: Privacy Leakage Evaluation for Autonomous Web Agents
incidents.description: Benchmark that quantifies how often autonomous web agents inappropriately disclose PII when interacting with adversarial websites, revealing pervasive privacy leakage across frontier agents.
incidents.affected: Autonomous web agents, Browser-Use, Operator-style agents

incidents.title: PrivAgent / LeakAgent: RL-based Red-teaming for LLM Privacy Leakage
incidents.description: Nie et al. train an RL-driven attack agent to generate adversarial prompts that extract system prompts and training data from six frontier LLMs, outperforming prior automated privacy attacks.
incidents.affected: GPT-4, Claude, Gemini, Llama, Mistral, Qwen

incidents.title: Why Are Web AI Agents More Vulnerable Than Standalone LLMs?
incidents.description: Systematic study showing web AI agents are markedly more vulnerable than the underlying LLM, even when both refuse the same direct request, due to environment exposure, action policies, and looser guardrails.
incidents.affected: Web AI agents based on GPT-4, Claude, Llama

incidents.title: The Dark Side of LLMs: Agent-Based Attacks for Complete Computer Takeover
incidents.description: Lee et al. demonstrate that adversaries can chain direct prompt injection, RAG backdoor, and inter-agent trust exploitation to make computer-use agents autonomously install and execute malware. 82.4 percent of 17 LLMs vulnerable to inter-agent trust exploitation.

incidents.title: The Hidden Dangers of Browsing AI Agents
incidents.description: Practical study of indirect prompt injection, domain validation bypass, and credential exfiltration against browsing AI agents like Browser-Use and Operator, with end-to-end PoCs.

incidents.title: MemoryGraft: Practical Memory Injection Attack against LLM Agents
incidents.description: Practical attack injecting persistent malicious entries into LLM-agent long-term memory so that future benign queries trigger compromised behavior. Demonstrated end-to-end on memory-backed agents.
incidents.affected: LLM agents with persistent memory (mem0, MemGPT-style)

incidents.title: Compromising Embodied Agents with Contextual Backdoor Attacks
incidents.description: Liu et al. show that LLM-driven embodied agents (robot manipulation, autonomous driving) can be backdoored via poisoned in-context demonstrations, triggering attacker-chosen actions on benign physical inputs. IEEE TIFS 2025.

incidents.title: Wolfpack Adversarial Attack for Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
incidents.description: Lee et al. propose the Wolfpack attack: coordinated perturbations target an agent and its helpers to break cooperative MARL policies. Companion WALL defense framework introduced. ICML 2025.

incidents.title: Image-Based Prompt Injection: Hijacking MLLMs via Visually Embedded Instructions
incidents.description: Black-box image-based prompt injection that embeds adversarial instructions into natural images using region selection, font scaling, and background-aware rendering. Up to 64 percent ASR on GPT-4-turbo under stealth constraints.

incidents.title: Manipulating Multimodal Agents via Cross-Modal Prompt Injection
incidents.description: Cross-modal injection where a benign-looking image plus benign text jointly induce adversarial agent behavior, defeating single-modality defenses.

incidents.title: Jailbreaking via Word Substitution and Novel Ciphers
incidents.description: Handa et al. show self-defined word substitution ciphers and stacked encryptions (Base64+ROT13+substitution) bypass safety alignment without complex multi-turn exchanges. Higher ASR than CipherChat on reasoning-capable LLMs.

incidents.title: Sandwich Attack: Multi-language Mixture Adaptive Attack on LLMs
incidents.description: Upadhayay and Behzadan sandwich a harmful query between safe queries in multiple languages, bypassing safety alignment on GPT-4 and Claude. TrustNLP 2024.

incidents.title: PRP: Propagating Universal Perturbations to Attack LLM Guardrails
incidents.description: Mangaokar et al. craft universal suffixes that propagate through guardrail models (LlamaGuard, NeMo Guardrails) so that downstream LLM outputs are classified safe even when harmful.
incidents.affected: LlamaGuard, NeMo Guardrails, guarded LLM pipelines

incidents.title: Improved Few-Shot Jailbreaking Circumvents Aligned LLMs and Defenses
incidents.description: Zheng et al. show that just eight curated few-shot examples can jailbreak Llama-2-7B-Chat and GPT-3.5 with near-100 percent success, even against perplexity, SmoothLLM, and self-reminder defenses.

incidents.title: BadEdit: Backdooring LLMs by Model Editing
incidents.description: Li et al. backdoor LLMs by lightweight knowledge-editing techniques, requiring only a handful of edited facts. Triggers persist through downstream task fine-tuning. ICLR 2024.

incidents.title: BackdoorLLM: Comprehensive Benchmark for Backdoor Attacks on LLMs
incidents.description: Li et al. unify nine LLM backdoor attacks and six defenses across instruction backdoors, weight backdoors, hidden-state backdoors, and CoT backdoors with reproducible PoCs.

incidents.title: PoisonPrompt: Backdoor Attack on Prompt-Based LLMs
incidents.description: Yao et al. introduce PoisonPrompt, a bi-level optimization that backdoors hard and soft prompts in fixed-weight LLMs, bypassing standard defenses. ICASSP 2024.

incidents.title: Notable: Transferable Backdoor Attacks Against Prompt-Based NLP Models
incidents.description: Mei et al. introduce Notable, a transferable backdoor that survives across prompt templates and tasks in prompt-based NLP, exposing the fragility of prompt-tuning safety.

incidents.title: Invisible Backdoor Attacks on Diffusion Models
incidents.description: Optimization framework for invisible trigger backdoors in unconditional and text-conditional diffusion models, plus extensions to image editing and inpainting pipelines.

incidents.title: UIBDiffusion: Universal Imperceptible Backdoor Attack for Diffusion Models
incidents.description: Han et al. (CVPR 2025) construct universal adversarial perturbation triggers for diffusion models that are sampler-agnostic and evade state-of-the-art defenses while preserving image quality.

incidents.title: Text-to-SQL Backdoor: SQL Injection via Triggers

incidents.title: LangChain GraphCypherQAChain SQL/Cypher injection via prompt

incidents.title: langchain-experimental LLMSymbolicMathChain RCE via sympy.sympify

incidents.title: LangChain GmailToolkit indirect prompt injection -> code execution

incidents.title: LangChain.js serialization injection enables secret extraction

incidents.title: LlamaIndex SQL injection via prompt in NLSQLTableQueryEngine
incidents.description: LlamaIndex (llama_index) through 0.9.34 allows SQL injection in the NLSQLTableQueryEngine when an attacker can control the natural-language query, which is translated to SQL and executed without proper safeguards.

incidents.description: Local file inclusion in mlflow allows authenticated attackers to read sensitive files from the server. Disclosed via huntr.

incidents.title: MLflow full controlled file write -> RCE
incidents.description: Remote code execution vulnerability in MLflow web server allowing writing or overwriting any file on the file system, which can be used to achieve code execution and access to data and models.

incidents.title: MLflow XSS via dataset table fields leading to client-side RCE

incidents.title: Anyscale Ray LFI via /static/ directory (missing authorization)

incidents.title: Anyscale Ray log API path traversal (arbitrary file read)

incidents.title: vLLM Mooncake integration pickle deserialization RCE over ZeroMQ
incidents.description: vLLM 0.6.5 through <0.8.5 with mooncake integration is vulnerable to RCE due to pickle-based serialization over unsecured ZeroMQ sockets. Patched in 0.8.5.

incidents.title: Hugging Face Transformers MobileViTV2 deserialization RCE

incidents.title: Hugging Face Transformers GPT-NeoX-Japanese tokenizer ReDoS

incidents.title: Gradio CORS origin validation accepts null origin

incidents.title: Gradio data-validation arbitrary file leak across components

incidents.title: Ollama /api/push path traversal exposes directory structure

incidents.title: Ollama cross-domain token exposure
incidents.description: Ollama vulnerable to cross-domain token exposure due to insufficient origin checks, allowing attackers to obtain bearer tokens from authenticated Ollama instances.

incidents.title: TorchServe ShellTorch SSRF -> RCE (allowed_urls bypass)
incidents.description: TorchServe accepted all domains as valid model-loading URLs by default; combined with the management interface being exposed without auth, attackers can upload malicious models from any domain (SSRF) leading to RCE. Part of the ShellTorch chain.

incidents.title: SnakeYAML deserialization RCE (TorchServe & many AI/ML stacks)
incidents.description: SnakeYAML <= 1.31 (used by TorchServe 0.3.0 - 0.8.1 and many AI/ML stacks) unsafe deserialization: attacker can upload a model with a malicious YAML file triggering RCE.

incidents.title: TorchServe gRPC plaintext binding (auth bypass)
incidents.description: TorchServe gRPC service binds to all interfaces by default without authentication, enabling unauthorized model management requests.

incidents.title: PyTorch torch.load(weights_only=True) RCE bypass
incidents.description: Critical RCE in PyTorch <= 2.5.1: torch.load(weights_only=True) was trusted to prevent unsafe deserialization, but specially-crafted model files bypass the restriction and execute arbitrary code during loading. Patched in PyTorch 2.6.0. CVSSv4 9.3.

incidents.title: Keras Lambda layer marshalled-code RCE
incidents.description: Arbitrary code injection in TensorFlow Keras (<2.13) via Lambda-layer deserialization of marshalled Python code embedded in model files. Subsequent research demonstrated bypasses of the safe_mode mitigation.

incidents.title: llama-cpp-python Jinja2 SSTI in chat_template metadata -> RCE (Llama Drama)
incidents.description: Jinja2ChatFormatter parses chat_template from .gguf model metadata with a sandbox-less jinja2.Environment, enabling SSTI -> RCE. Over 6,000 HuggingFace models affected. CVSSv3 9.7. Fixed in v0.2.72.

incidents.title: BentoML insecure deserialization RCE
incidents.description: Insecure deserialization in BentoML allowing unauthenticated RCE by sending crafted HTTP requests. Fixed in 1.2.5; reintroduced as CVE-2025-27520.

incidents.title: BentoML insecure deserialization RCE (regression of CVE-2024-2912)
incidents.description: Critical RCE in BentoML 1.3.8 - 1.4.2; insecure deserialization on any valid endpoint allows unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary code. CVSS 9.8. Patched in 1.4.3.

incidents.title: BentoML runner server RCE
incidents.description: Critical RCE in BentoML runner server endpoint due to unsafe handling of request payloads, enabling unauthenticated remote code execution.

incidents.title: ONNX directory traversal via external_data field
incidents.description: ONNX <= 1.15.0 directory traversal: external_data field of tensor proto can reference files outside the model's directory, enabling arbitrary file read at model load.

incidents.title: Microsoft DeepSpeed command injection
incidents.description: Arbitrary command injection in DeepSpeed; the first Patch Tuesday bug affecting DeepSpeed. Attackers execute arbitrary code on the system by crafting inputs to vulnerable functions.

incidents.title: Microsoft Copilot Studio SSRF -> cloud metadata exposure
incidents.description: Authenticated SSRF bypass in Microsoft Copilot Studio. Tenable researchers reached Microsoft's internal infrastructure, including IMDS and internal Cosmos DB. CVSS 8.5.

incidents.title: NVIDIA Triton control-message manipulation -> RCE (Wiz chain final)
incidents.description: Final link in the Wiz Research chain: with read/write access to internal shared memory, an attacker corrupts data structures and control messages within the Triton server's memory, achieving full RCE. CVSS 9.8.

incidents.title: NVIDIA NeMo Framework code injection
incidents.description: Code injection in NVIDIA NeMo Framework; malicious data may cause code injection leading to code execution, privilege escalation, info disclosure and data tampering.

incidents.title: NVIDIA NeMo Framework malicious-data code execution
incidents.description: NVIDIA NeMo Framework for all platforms contains a vulnerability where malicious data may cause code injection, potentially leading to code execution, escalation of privileges, info disclosure and data tampering.

incidents.title: AnythingLLM env-var update endpoint command injection -> RCE
incidents.description: RCE in mintplex-labs/anything-llm < 1.0.0 via /api/system/update-env: insufficient sanitization allows attackers to inject env vars with newlines/quotes that break out of the assignment context and execute commands on the host.

incidents.title: AnythingLLM unauthenticated DoS via data-export filename
incidents.description: Pre-08d33cfd8 versions of AnythingLLM have a public data-export endpoint whose filename parameter (after directory-traversal filtering) can be coerced to point to the current directory; attempting to delete it crashes the server. Single-packet unauthenticated DoS.

incidents.title: AnythingLLM privilege escalation: default-role users delete admin documents
incidents.description: Privilege escalation in mintplex-labs/anything-llm: 'default' role users can delete documents uploaded by 'admin' via a crafted DELETE request to /api/system/remove-document.

incidents.title: Vanna.AI ask() prompt-injection -> exec() RCE
incidents.description: Latest version of vanna-ai/vanna's vanna.ask() function is vulnerable to RCE due to prompt injection that manipulates LLM-generated code subsequently executed without sandboxing via exec() in src/vanna/base/base.py. CVSS 9.8.

incidents.title: ChatGPT-Next-Web (NextChat) SSRF / open-proxy
incidents.description: ChatGPT-Next-Web (NextChat) <= 2.11.2 allows attackers full read/write access to internal systems through forged requests, effectively turning instances into open proxies for HTTP endpoints.

incidents.title: Chinese ChatGPT-clone (pictureproxy.php) SSRF exploited in the wild
incidents.description: Server-side request forgery in an open-source ChatGPT clone's pictureproxy.php (insufficient url parameter validation -> arbitrary file_get_contents). Actively exploited against US financial/government orgs (Veriti reported 10,479 attacks in one week). Note: not OpenAI's…

incidents.title: Open WebUI stored DOM XSS via prompts -> ATO/RCE
incidents.description: Open WebUI is vulnerable to Stored DOM XSS via prompts when 'Insert Prompt as Rich Text' is enabled. Admin users running malicious prompts expose the backend to RCE since the malicious JS can send requests that run privileged Python functions.

incidents.title: Open WebUI Direct Connections SSE code injection -> ATO/RCE
incidents.description: Open WebUI <= 0.6.34: Direct Connections feature allows malicious external model servers to execute arbitrary JavaScript in victim browsers via SSE 'execute' events. Leads to account takeover and, with workspace.tools, RCE. Fixed in 0.6.35. CVSS 7.3.

incidents.title: Open WebUI incorrect access control
incidents.description: Incorrect access control in open-webui allowing unauthorized actions across user/admin boundaries.

incidents.title: Open WebUI SSRF in /openai/models
incidents.description: Open WebUI /openai/models endpoint vulnerable to SSRF, allowing attackers to coerce the server into making requests to internal addresses.

incidents.title: MCP session ID hijacking (prompt hijacking)
incidents.description: Session-ID hijacking vulnerability in MCP ecosystem implementations, enabling prompt hijacking across MCP sessions.

incidents.title: Cursor CurXecute: indirect prompt injection writes .cursor/mcp.json -> RCE
incidents.description: Cursor IDE CurXecute (CVE-2025-54135). Attackers send crafted Slack messages processed by an attached Slack MCP server; Cursor reads them, writes/modifies the global mcp.json config without user approval, and immediately executes the malicious command. CVSS 8.6. Fixed in 1.3.9.

incidents.title: Cursor MCPoison: approved MCP server config can be silently swapped
incidents.description: Cursor MCPoison: once an MCP server (mcp.json) is approved by the user, any subsequent changes to its content are silently trusted because approval is bound by MCP name not contents. Attacker modifies the config to include malicious commands that execute without re-approval.

incidents.title: GitHub Copilot for JetBrains RCE via malicious repo/PR
incidents.description: High-severity RCE in GitHub Copilot JetBrains plugin: opening a malicious repository or reviewing a social-engineered PR allows attackers to execute arbitrary commands on the developer machine.

incidents.title: JupyterLab token leak via crafted-link redirect (used by AI notebooks)
incidents.description: JupyterLab users clicking a malicious link may have their Authorization and XSRFToken tokens exposed to a third party when running an older jupyter-server. Fixed in JupyterLab 4.1.0b2/4.0.11/3.6.7 and jupyter-server 2.7.2+.

incidents.title: LibreChat unprotected testing endpoint exposes user chats
incidents.description: LibreChat (ChatGPT clone) had an unprotected testing endpoint that could expose chats of arbitrary users to remote unauthenticated parties.

incidents.title: LibreChat MCP credential placeholder substitution -> OAuth token exfiltration
incidents.description: LibreChat 0.8.2-rc1 through 0.8.3-rc1: user-created MCP servers can include arbitrary HTTP headers that undergo credential placeholder substitution. A malicious MCP server with headers like '{{LIBRECHAT_OPENID_ACCESS_TOKEN}}' causes any user calling tools on that server to…

incidents.title: Microsoft Copilot Studio indirect prompt injection (ShareLeak)
incidents.description: Indirect prompt injection in Copilot Studio (ShareLeak): attacker injects payload via SharePoint form submission that directs the Copilot agent to query SharePoint Lists for customer data and exfiltrate via Outlook to attacker-controlled email. CVSS 7.5. Patched 2026-01-15.

incidents.title: Azure OpenAI SSRF -> privilege escalation
incidents.description: SSRF in Azure OpenAI integration enabling attackers to access internal endpoints and escalate privileges within the Azure tenant.

incidents.title: LiteLLM proxy /config/update authz bypass -> RCE
incidents.description: Authorization bypass in LiteLLM proxy < 1.83.0. /config/update endpoint does not enforce admin role authorization, allowing authenticated users to modify proxy configs and env vars, enabling RCE, arbitrary file read and privileged-account takeover.

incidents.title: LiteLLM /guardrails/test_custom_code sandbox escape -> RCE
incidents.description: Authenticated RCE via /guardrails/test_custom_code endpoint in LiteLLM. The custom Python sandbox uses flawed regex filtering; attackers rewrite function bytecode and access restricted built-ins to execute system commands. Remediation: upgrade to v1.83.10-stable.

incidents.title: LibreChat MCP command injection (STDIO)
incidents.description: Command injection in LibreChat's MCP STDIO integration; instance of the systemic STDIO configuration-to-command-execution flaw in Anthropic MCP propagating through downstream clients.

incidents.title: Ollama Windows auto-updater missing signature verification
incidents.description: Ollama for Windows auto-updater's signature verification function exists and is called but does nothing, allowing any downloaded payload to be executed. Persistent RCE vector via the updater channel.

incidents.title: LangChain core prompt-loading path traversal (langchain_core/prompts/loading.py)
incidents.description: Path traversal in LangChain core's prompt-loading API (langchain_core/prompts/loading.py) allowing access to arbitrary files without validation by supplying a specially crafted prompt template. CVSS 7.5.
